attribution.note: These are Marcus's own words in his own Substack post. They conclude his numbered argument, which he presents as his own.

semantics.note: 'Will wind up overpaying' is firm, unhedged language. The chain's premise, that there is no moat, is asserted rather than offered as a hypothetical, so this is a plain forecast. Limiting 'everybody' to the competing AI builders matches the passage. No deadline was given.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary: eventual AI returns too small to justify the investment. Treating intense competition as part of the forecast fits the text. The contract's high bars for support and for contradiction are reasonable given the speaker gave no deadline or metric. The result does not turn on the interpretation.

evidence.note: Alphabet's Q2 2026 disclosure, available before the cutoff. It reports one quarter of negative free cash flow driven by capex and strong operating income. It does not show eventual returns on the AI investment.

Microsoft's FY26 annual report, dated 2026-10-14. The CEO says he is confident in long-term returns. That is management's expectation, not a realized counterexample, and record company-wide results are not AI-specific returns.

Anthropic's S-1, dated 2026-10-26. It discloses net losses and a profitability risk factor. The losses are largely changes in fair value of notes. A risk disclosure about one firm does not show completed overpayment across the group.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline about eventual AI investment returns. The packet holds only interim, company-level context: Alphabet's quarterly cash flow, Microsoft's management confidence, and Anthropic's losses and risk factors. None of it shows completed returns across the group, and none shows a firm whose realized AI returns justify its investment. No conclusive event has occurred, so the claim cannot be scored yet.
